newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods head downhill with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods head downhill with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices, led by gasoline, took a beating by late Thursday afternoon tracking lower NYMEX futures and soft differentials, traders said.
Gasoline fell about two cents a gallon as supplies abounded amid continuing strong domestic output and the pervasive trend toward minimal just-in-time inventories, traders said.
Profit-taking was reportedly the key to the distillate drop, which slid as much as 1.75 cents a gallon.

News was otherwise scarce, they said, and dealings were thin on cash markets. Traders noted the current NYMEX heat and gasoline backwardation has limited spot buying interest, particularly during this period between peak-demand seasons.
In New York Harbor, heating oil and low sulfur diesel offers were static, with prompt September heat pegged at about even with the screen.
Conventional gasoline values eased to about 1.50 cents under the NYMEX print, while prompt regular RFG slipped to about 0.15 cent over the print.
Traders said talk of an increase in gasoline charters to the U.S. contributed to the weakness.
